[p. 444]

Surah "Al-Mujadilah" (The Pleader)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of she who pleads with you﴾, she who argues with you. It was also recited with it. She was Khawla bint Tha'laba, the wife of Aws ibn al-Samit, brother of Ubada. He saw her while she was praying, and she was beautiful of body. When she finished her prayer, he made advances to her, but she refused. He became angry and declared her unlawful to himself through zihar (the pre-Islamic practice of a husband declaring his wife forbidden to him by likening her to his mother). She came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Aws married me when I was young and desirable. When my years had passed and my belly had given birth, that is, my children had multiplied, he made me to him like his mother." It is also narrated that she said: "I have young children. If I entrust them to him, they will be lost, and if I take them to myself, they will go hungry." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have no ruling concerning your matter." It is also narrated that he said to her: "You have become forbidden to him." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, he did not mention divorce. He is the father of my children and the most beloved of people to me." He said: "You have become forbidden to him." She said: "I complain to Allah of my poverty and my grief." Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have become forbidden to him," she cried out and complained. So it was revealed ﴿concerning her husband﴾, regarding his affair. Its meaning is ﴿and complains to Allah﴾, displays what she suffers of distress.

﴿And Allah hears your exchange﴾, (p. 445) your mutual discussion of words, from "hara", meaning he returned.

﴿Indeed Allah is All-Hearing﴾, who hears the complaint of the distressed one,

﴿All-Seeing﴾, of his condition.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 2:

﴿Those of you who make their wives unlawful to themselves by saying "you are to me like the back of my mother" (alladhina yuzahiruna)﴾. ʿĀṣim read "yuẓahirūna" (with the ẓāʾ in the form yuẓahhirūna), while the people of the Ḥijāz and Baṣra read it as "yuẓāhirūna"; others read "yaẓẓāharūna" (ẓihār, the pre-Islamic form of divorce by likening a wife to one's mother). The phrase ﴿minkum﴾ ("of you") is a reproach to the Arabs, because this oath (zihar) was among the oaths of the people of their pre-Islamic age in particular, not among the other nations.

﴿min nisāʾihim﴾ (from their women): i.e., their wives.

﴿mā hunna ummahātihim﴾ (they are not their mothers). "ummahātuhum" (their mothers) is read with the superlative form, ("al-mufaḍḍal"), the first being Ḥijāzī and the second Tamīmī.

﴿in ummahātuhum illā allāʾī waladnahum﴾ (their mothers are none other than those who bore them). He means that mothers in the true sense are the ones who gave birth, and nursing mothers are attached to the birth-mothers by means of suckling. Likewise are the wives of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), for the increase of their sanctity. As for wives, they are the furthest thing from motherhood; therefore He says: ﴿wa innahum la-yaqūlūna munkaran mina al-qawli﴾ (and indeed they utter an objectionable word and a falsehood), which the reality and the legal rulings deny.

﴿wa zūran﴾ (and falsehood), and lies, vanity, deviating from the truth.

﴿wa inna Allāha la-ʿafuwwun ghafūr﴾ (and indeed God is Pardoning, Forgiving), for what has passed of them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 3:

﴿Those who make zihar (a pre-Islamic form of divorce by likening one's wife to a forbidden female relative) against their wives﴾. In the first verse he explained that this is, from the one who says it, a reprehensible and false statement. In the second he explained the ruling on zihar.

﴿Then they retract what they said﴾. Al-'awd (returning) means becoming something, either at the outset or by continuing. The first sense is found in His saying: ﴿until it became like an old, withered palm stalk﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:39], and the second in: ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾ [al-Isra 17:8]. It is used transitively, as in your saying "'uduhu" (I returned to him) when you came to him and went to him, and with prepositions: "ila" (to), "'ala" (upon), "fi" (in), and the lam (for), as in His saying: ﴿And even if they were returned, they would revert to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am 6:28]. From this is His saying: ﴿then they retract what they said﴾, meaning: they return to annul what they said, or to rectify it, with an elided noun (idmar al-mudaf). It is also reported from Tha'labah: "they return to make lawful what they made unlawful," again with an elided noun. However, he meant by "what they said" what they had made unlawful for themselves, by the wording of zihar, treating the saying as if it were the thing said about, as in His saying: ﴿and We will inherit from him what he says﴾ [Maryam 19:80], where he meant the thing spoken about, which is wealth and children. Then they differed over what annulment is achieved by. According to us, it is by the resolve to have intercourse, and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), al-Hasan and Qatadah. According to al-Shafi'i, it is by mere retention, which means not divorcing her immediately after the zihar.

﴿Then the freeing of a neck (tahrir raqabah)﴾. He must free a believing or a non-believing slave. It is not valid to use a mudabbar (a slave whose freedom is promised upon the master's death), an umm walad (a slave woman who has borne her master's child), or a mukatab (a slave who has contracted to buy his freedom and has paid something of it).

﴿Before they touch one another﴾. The pronoun refers to what the context indicates, namely the one who makes zihar and the wife he made zihar against. Al-mumassah (touching) means enjoying her sexually: by intercourse, by touching with desire, or by looking at her private part with desire.

﴿That is﴾: the ruling.

﴿by which you are admonished﴾: because the ruling of expiation is evidence that the offence was committed, so you must take heed from this ruling, so that you do not return to zihar and fear the punishment of Allah for it.

﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾. Zihar is for a man to say to his wife: "You are to me like the back of my mother." If he puts in the place of "you" a part of her body by which the whole is expressed, or in place of "the back" another member that it is forbidden to look at in the case of the mother, such as the belly or the thigh, or in place of "mother" a woman who is a mahram (forbidden in marriage) to him by blood, by fosterage, by marital relation, or by intercourse, such as saying: "You are to me like the back of my foster sister," or "my paternal aunt," or "my son's wife," or "my wife's mother," or "her daughter," then he is a mudahhir (one who makes zihar). If the one making zihar refrains from expiation, the wife may bring the matter to a judge, and the judge must compel him to expiate and may imprison him. No expiation is enforced by compulsion and imprisonment except the expiation of zihar, because it harms her through his refusal to expiate and his refraining from enjoying her. If he touches her before expiating, he should seek Allah's forgiveness and must not return to her until he has expiated. If he frees part of the neck and then touches her, he must begin again, according to Abu Hanifah (may Allah have mercy on him).

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 58, verse 4:**

﴿So whoever does not find﴾ the *raqabah* (a slave),

﴿then fasting two months﴾: then it is incumbent upon him to fast two months,

﴿consecutively, before they touch each other. So whoever is not able﴾ [to fast],

﴿then feeding﴾: then it is incumbent upon him to feed

﴿sixty needy persons﴾, for each needy person half a *sa'* of wheat, or a *sa'* of something other than it. He must pay this before the *masis* (intercourse), but he does not have to begin again if he has intercourse during the feeding.

﴿That﴾, i.e., the clarification and the teaching of the rulings,

﴿so that you may believe﴾, so that you may affirm,

﴿in Allah and His Messenger﴾, by acting upon the laws He prescribed, including *zihar* (the pre-Islamic practice of declaring one's wife unlawful to oneself by likening her to one's mother) and others, and by abandoning what you used to do in your pre-Islamic ignorance.

﴿And these﴾, i.e., the rulings which We described (p-447) regarding *zihar* and expiation,

﴿are the limits of Allah﴾, which it is not permissible to transgress,

﴿and for the disbelievers﴾, those who do not follow them,

﴿is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., painful.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 5:

﴿Indeed, those who oppose (yuhadduna) Allah and His Messenger﴾: they show enmity (ya'addun) and oppose (yushaqqun),

﴿will be humiliated (kubitu)﴾: they will be disgraced and destroyed,

﴿just as those before them were humiliated﴾: from among the enemies of the messengers,

﴿And We have sent down clear signs﴾: which point to the truthfulness of the Messenger and the soundness of what he brought,

﴿and for the disbelievers﴾: by these signs,

﴿is a humiliating punishment﴾: which will strip them of their might and their arrogance.

﴿يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ﴾ ["on the Day when He resurrects them"]: this is in the accusative (manṣūb) because it is governed by "muhīn" (humiliating), or by an implied "udhkur" ("remember"), to magnify the Day.

﴿اللهُ جَمِيعًا﴾ ["Allah, all of them"]: all of them, without leaving out any one of them from being resurrected, or (they will be) gathered together in one state.

﴿فَيُنَبِّئُهم بِما عَمِلُوا﴾ ["then He will inform them of what they did"]: to shame them, to rebuke them, and to expose their condition. They will wish, at that moment, to be hastened into the Fire, because of the disgrace that will befall them before all the witnesses.

﴿أحْصاهُ اللهُ﴾ ["Allah has enumerated it"]: He has encompassed it in number, so nothing of it has escaped Him.

﴿وَنَسُوهُ﴾ ["and they forgot it"]: because they were careless about it when they committed it, and only important matters are kept in memory.

﴿واللهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾ ["and Allah is Witness over all things"]: nothing is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 7:

﴿Have you not considered that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth?﴾ "Yakūnu" (يَكُونُ) is from "kāna" (كانَ), the complete (tāmma) usage, meaning: "what occurs."

﴿Of a private conversation among three﴾: "al-najwā" (النَّجْوى) is the private conversing (al-tanājī). It is idafa (annexed) to "thalātha" (ثَلاثَةٍ), meaning: "of a private conversation among three persons."

﴿except that He is﴾, i.e., Allah,

﴿the fourth of them, nor of five except that He is the sixth of them, nor of what is less than that, nor more, except that He is with them﴾, knowing what they converse about, and nothing of what they are engaged in is hidden from Him. He is exalted far above being in a place. The specification of three and five is because the verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites, who used to gather for private conversation to enrage the believers, using these two numbers. It is also said: no three of them converse privately, nor five, nor fewer than their number, nor more, except that Allah is with them, hearing (p-448) what they say. And because those who converse privately are customarily a group of people of opinion and experience, the smallest number of them is two, and then it goes up to three, to five, to six, to whatever the situation requires. So He, Mighty and Exalted, mentioned three and five and said "nor of what is less than that," which indicates two and four, and said "nor more," which indicates what approaches this number.

﴿Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection﴾, and will recompense them for it.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 8:

﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret consultation, and then they return to what they were forbidden, and they consult together in sin, and enmity, and disobedience to the Messenger?﴾ The Jews and the hypocrites used to consult together among themselves, and they would wink at one another with their eyes when they saw the believers. They intended to vex them, and by their consultation and winking they gave the impression that their raiders had been defeated and that their relatives had been killed. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade them, but they returned to the same behaviour. Their consultation was about what is sin and enmity toward the believers, and a mutual agreement to disobey the Messenger and oppose him. It is also read as "wa-yatanajjawna" (وَيَتَنَجَّوْنَ), with the reading of Hamzah, and it has the same meaning as the first.

﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with what Allah has not greeted you with﴾. That is, they say in their greeting to you: "As-sam 'alayka" (اَلسّامُ عَلَيْكَ). "As-sam" means "death". Allah (Exalted) says: ﴿And peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾ [al-Naml: 59]. They would say "Ya ayyuha al-Rasul" (يا أيُّها الرَسُولُ) and "Ya ayyuha al-Nabi" (يا أيُّها النَبِيُّ).

﴿And they say to themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ That is, they say among themselves: "If he were a prophet, Allah would punish us for what we say." So Allah (Exalted) says: ﴿Hell is sufficient for them as a punishment﴾,

﴿they will burn in it﴾, a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: they will enter it,

﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, i.e. the place of return, Hell.

O you who believe, (with their tongues), and this is an address to the hypocrites, though the apparent meaning is that it is an address to the believers.

﴿When you hold private consultation, do not consult together in sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger﴾. That is: when you hold private consultation, do not imitate the Jews and the hypocrites in their private consultations concerning evil.

﴿But consult together in righteousness﴾, by performing the obligatory duties and acts of obedience,

﴿and piety﴾, and by abandoning sins.

﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾, (p-449) for reckoning, so that He will recompense you for whatever good or evil you consult about.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 10:

﴿Secret counsel is only from Satan﴾, [meaning it is] with sin and transgression,

﴿from Satan﴾, [meaning it is] from his adornment [of it],

﴿so that he may grieve﴾, i.e., Satan, and with a dammah on the yā' [i.e., yuḥzana], [this is the reading of] Nāfi',

﴿those who believe; but he cannot harm them at all﴾, Satan, or the grief,

﴿except by Allah's permission﴾, [meaning] by His knowledge, His decree, and His predestination,

﴿and upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, i.e., they entrust their affairs to Allah and seek refuge in Him from Satan.

"O you who have believed, when you are told, 'Make room (tafassahu) in the assemblies,'" — widen (tawassa'u) therein — "in the assemblies." Asim and Nafi' read it as "fi al-majalis" (in the assemblies, in the plural).

The intended assembly is the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they used to crowd together in it out of eagerness to be near him and keen to hear his words. It was also said: it refers to an assembly of battle, that is, the positions of the warriors, as in His saying: ﴿positions for the fighting﴾ [Al 'Imran: 121]. Muqatil said: it refers to the Friday prayer.

﴿Then make room (fafsahu)﴾: then widen.

﴿Allah will make room for you (yafsah Allahu lakum)﴾: this is unrestricted, covering everything that people seek room in, whether of place, provision, breast (chest), grave, and other things.

﴿And when you are told, "Rise up (unshuzu)"﴾: stand up, to make room for those who come. Or: rise up from the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when you are commanded to rise from it. Or: rise up to prayer, jihad, and works of goodness.

﴿Then rise up (fa-unshuzu)﴾: with the damma in both places, read by Madani, Shami, and Asim except Hammad.

﴿Allah will raise those of you who have believed﴾: by complying with His commands and the commands of His Messenger,

﴿and those who have been given knowledge﴾: and especially the scholars among them,

﴿by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾: regarding the "degrees," there are two views. One is in this world, in rank and honour; the other is in the Hereafter. It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that when he recited it he would say: "O people, understand this verse, and let it encourage you toward knowledge." And from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the full moon on its night over the rest of the stars." And from him (ﷺ): "The worship of the scholar for one day equals the worship of the worshipper for forty years." And from him (ﷺ): "Three will intercede on the Day of Resurrection: the prophets, then the scholars, then the martyrs." How great is a rank that lies between prophethood and martyrdom, by the testimony of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!

And from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "Sulayman (peace be upon him) was given the choice between knowledge, wealth, and kingship, and he chose knowledge, and wealth and kingship were given to him along with it." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah revealed to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'O Ibrahim, I am 'Alim (All-Knowing), and I love every 'alim (knowing person).'" And from some of the wise: "Would that I knew what he who has attained knowledge has gained, and what he who has attained knowledge has missed." And from al-Zubayri: "Knowledge is masculine, so only the manhood of men loves it."

Sciences are of various kinds, and the most noble of them is the most noble in its object of knowledge.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 12:**

﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger﴾: when you wish to speak privately with him (munajat).

﴿then present before your consultation a charity﴾: i.e., before your private consultation. This is a metaphor (isti'arah) from one who has hands, like the saying of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "Among the finest things the Arabs were given is poetry. A man presents it before his need, so he seeks rain from the generous through it, and brings down the stingy through it." He means: "before his need."

﴿That﴾: the presenting.

﴿is better for you﴾: in your religion.

﴿and purer﴾: because charity is a purification.

﴿And purer. But if you do not find﴾: [anything] that you can give in charity.

﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: for permitting private consultation without charity. It is said that this lasted ten nights and was then abrogated (nasakha, naskh: the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation). It is also said that it was only an hour of a day, and then it was abrogated. ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "This is a verse from the Book of Allah that no one acted upon before me and no one will act upon after me. I had a dinar, which I exchanged, and whenever I wished to consult him I gave a dirham in charity. I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ten questions, and he answered them for me. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is fidelity (al-wafa')?' He said: 'Monotheism (al-tawhid) and the testimony that there is no god but Allah.' I said: 'And what is corruption (al-fasad)?' He said: 'Disbelief (al-kufr) and associating partners with Allah (al-shirk).' I said: 'And what is the truth (al-haqq)?' He said: 'Islam, the Qur'an, and the guardianship (al-wilayah) when it reaches you.' I said: 'And what is stratagem (al-hilah)?' He said: 'Leaving off stratagem.' I said: 'And what is incumbent upon me?' He said: 'Obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger.' I said: 'And how should I call upon Allah (Exalted is He)?' He said: 'With truthfulness and certainty.' I said: 'And what should I ask Allah for?' He said: 'Well-being (al-'afiyah).' (p-٤٥١) I said: 'And what should I do for the salvation of my soul?' He said: 'Eat what is lawful and speak the truth.' I said: 'And what is joy (al-surur)?' He said: 'Paradise.' I said: 'And what is comfort (al-rahah)?' He said: 'Meeting Allah.' When I finished with them, its abrogation was revealed."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 13:

﴿Are you afraid to offer charity before your private consultation (najwa)?﴾ Did you fear offering the charity because of the spending in it that you dislike?! ﴿So when you did not do it﴾, that which you were commanded to do, and it was hard upon you,

﴿and Allah has forgiven you﴾, i.e., He lightened it for you and removed from you the blame for leaving off offering charity before the private consultation, just as He removed the blame for the sin from the one who repents of it.

﴿So establish prayer, give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, i.e., do not neglect the prayer, the zakat, and the rest of the acts of obedience.

﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, and this is both a promise and a warning.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 14:

﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah is angry?﴾ The hypocrites (munafiqun) used to take the Jews as allies, and they are the ones with whom Allah is angry, in His saying: ﴿Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He is angry﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 60], and they would convey to them the secrets of the believers,

﴿They are not of you﴾, O Muslims,

﴿nor of them﴾, nor of the Jews, like His saying: ﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾ [al-Nisa': 143]. ﴿And they swear by a lie﴾, i.e., they say: "By Allah, we are indeed Muslims, not hypocrites,"

﴿while they know﴾ that they are liars, hypocrites.

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment﴾: a kind of punishment, intensifying.

﴿Indeed, evil is what they used to do﴾: they were, in the past time, persisting in evil deeds, and this is a report of what will be said to them in the Hereafter.

﴿They have taken their oaths﴾, the false ones, ﴿as a shield﴾, a protection for their blood and their property. ﴿So they barred﴾ the people, amid their security and safety, ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, from His obedience and from belief in Him. ﴿For them there is a humiliating punishment﴾: He promised them the punishment that disgraces them, for their disbelief and their barring others, like His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar (others) from the way of Allah, We shall increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾ [an-Nahl: 88].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 17:

﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah.﴾ "Against Allah" means: from the punishment of Allah.

﴿Anything﴾ means: even a little, from "al-ighna'" (avail, substitution of benefit).

﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 18:

﴿On the Day when Allah raises them all up, then they will swear to Him﴾, that is, to Allah, in the Hereafter, that they were sincere in the world and were not hypocrites,

﴿as they swear to you﴾, in the world, to that effect,

﴿and they think that they﴾, in the world,

﴿are upon something﴾, of benefit, or they think that they are upon something of benefit by their false oaths, just as they benefited here,

﴿Verily, it is they who are the liars﴾, since their state was the same in the world and in the Hereafter.

﴿The Shaytan has gained mastery over them﴾, meaning he took control of them.

﴿So he caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah﴾. Shah al-Kirmani said: "The sign of the Shaytan's gaining mastery over the servant is that he keeps him busy with the upkeep of his outward self, with food, drink and clothing, and keeps his heart occupied away from reflecting on the favours and blessings of Allah and from giving thanks for them. He keeps his tongue occupied away from the remembrance of his Lord with lying, backbiting and slander, and keeps his inner mind (lubb) occupied away from reflection and vigilance by managing and accumulating worldly things."

﴿Those are the party of the Shaytan﴾, meaning his army (junduh).

﴿Indeed, the party of the Shaytan, they are the losers﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 58, verse 20:

﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger—those are among the most humiliated.﴾ [They are] among those who are the most abased of Allah's creation (exalted is He); you will not see anyone more abased than them.

God has decreed (in the Preserved Tablet):

"I shall surely prevail, I and My messengers," by proof and by the sword, or by one of the two.

"Indeed God is Powerful," nothing that He wills is beyond Him,

"Mighty," Victorious, not overcome.

(p-453) ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾. It is a second object of "tajid" (you find), or a circumstantial clause (hal), or an attribute of "qawman" (a people). "Tajid" here means "you encounter" (tusadif). On this reading,

﴿who oppose Allah﴾: they oppose Him and are hostile to Him,

﴿and His Messenger﴾. That is: it is impossible for you to find believing people who befriend the polytheists. What is meant is that such a thing should not be, and that it ought to be impossible, never to be found in any circumstance, as an intensification in warning against keeping away from the enemies of Allah, distancing oneself from them, and guarding against mixing with and associating with them. He increased this emphasis and intensity with His words: ﴿even if they were their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their kindred﴾, and with His words: ﴿Those, He has written faith into their hearts﴾, that is, He established it in them, and by contrasting His words "Those are the party of Satan" with His words "Those are the party of Allah."

﴿And He strengthened them with a spirit from Him﴾: that is, with a Book He sent down, in which is life for them. It is also permissible for the pronoun to refer to faith, meaning: with a spirit from faith, since it is in itself a spirit for the life of the hearts. It is related from al-Thawri that he said: "They used to see that it was revealed concerning those who keep company with the ruler." It is related from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad that al-Mansur met him, and when he recognized him he fled from him, and he recited it. Sahl said: "Whoever makes his faith sound and purifies his monotheism, he will not feel at ease with an innovator, nor sit with him, and he will show him enmity from himself. Whoever flatters an innovator, Allah will strip him of the sweetness of the Sunnah. Whoever answers an innovator seeking the honour or wealth of this world, Allah will humble him by that honour and make him poor by that wealth. Whoever smiles at an innovator, Allah will remove the light of faith from his heart. And whoever does not believe, let him test it."

﴿And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; Allah is pleased with them﴾, for their pure monotheism and their obedience,

﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾, for His great reward in the Hereafter, or for what He decreed for them in this world,

﴿Those are the party of Allah﴾: the helpers of His right and the guardians of His creation,

﴿Surely the party of Allah are the successful﴾: those who remain in everlasting bliss, who attain every beloved thing, and who are safe from every dreaded thing.
